source.title: Symmetric power functoriality for Hilbert modular forms
source.authors: James Newton and Jack A. Thorne
source.provenanceNote: The versioned HTML and parsed PDF were read through the browser. Several PDF screenshots failed and PDF bytes could not be obtained in the execution filesystem, so no hash or complete diagram inspection is claimed. Author/title and publication metadata agree; a line-by-line comparison with the published 65-page version is not complete.

summary: Partial source-routing checkpoint with 57 records: 34 theorem records, 14 constructions and 9 definitions; 1 pinned-library carrier, 8 already-planned items and 48 missing exact declarations assigned once each to seven existing proposed roadmap owners. The main Hilbert symmetric-power endpoint is already planned in ML.3. The extraction preserves the residual nature of Theorems 5.5/5.9, the different-weight companion, all nine hypotheses of Theorem 4.1 including p=2, and ordered auxiliary-place conditions. Internal patching, prior-paper closure and the exhaustive pinned audit remain explicit continuation work. No new roadmap, mathematical implementation or complete paper extraction is claimed.

S3.parameters: F totally real; p≥5 prime; 0<r<p; n=2r; ι:Qpbar≅C; π regular algebraic cuspidal on GL₂(A_F); v₀ a finite place.
hypotheses: π has weight zero; each π_v for v|p is an unramified twist of Steinberg.
q_{v₀}≡−1 mod p and π_{v₀} is tamely dihedral of order p.
The residual image contains a conjugate of SL₂(F_{p^a}) for some a>a₀(p), with a₀ from Lemma 2.3.
Every finite π_v with v∤p is potentially unramified.
S3.conventions: All determinant and Hodge–Tate formulas use the paper’s ε_p with HT(ε_p)=−1. The relation ρ~ρ′ at a non-p place is the BLGGT14 §1.3 local-component relation named in the paper, not equality of representations; its independent construction remains an imported obligation.

S5-global.parameters: F totally real; p≥5 prime; 0<r<p; ι:Qpbar≅C; π RAESDC on GL₂(A_F); φ_p an arithmetic Frobenius lift in G_Qp.
hypotheses: π has weight zero and each π_v for v|p is an unramified twist of Steinberg.
Some finite v₀ has q_{v₀}≡−1 mod p and π_{v₀} tamely dihedral of order p.
For every prime ℓ and every ι_ℓ:Qlbar≅C, the residual image contains a conjugate of SL₂(F_{ℓ^a}) for some ℓ^a>max(4r,5). At the fixed p,ι, it also contains SL₂(F_{p^a}) for some a>a₀(p).
Every finite π_v with v∤p is potentially unramified.

S5-local.parameters: F totally real; p≥5 prime; M>p^(a₀(p)); 0<r<p; ι:Qpbar≅C; π RAESDC on GL₂(A_F); φ_p an arithmetic Frobenius lift.
hypotheses: π has weight zero and each π_v for v|p is an unramified twist of Steinberg.
A finite place v₀ has q_{v₀}≡−1 mod p and π_{v₀} tamely dihedral of order p.
A finite place v₁ has q_{v₁}≡1 mod p and π_{v₁} an unramified twist of Steinberg.
Every finite π_v with v∤p and v≠v₁ is potentially unramified.
There are primes t₁,t₂>M and finite places w₁,w₂ of residue characteristics p₁,p₂>3 unramified in F, with π_{w_i} tamely dihedral of order t_i and p₁,p₂,t₁,t₂ all distinct.

H/F is the ray class field of modulus (8) times all infinite places. Let S consist of finite v≠w₁,w₂ for which π_v is ramified or F_v/Q is ramified, together with places above 2 or 3. The place w₁ splits in H F(S), and w₂ splits in H F(S∪{w₁}); F(T) is the maximal exponent-two abelian extension unramified at finite places outside T.
S5-local.conventions: Ramification of a place over Q means ramification of the local extension over its rational residue prime. F(T) permits ramification at real places: it is not stipulated to be totally real.

items.name: Underlying algebraic representation
items.statement: For a semiring k, monoid G and k-module V, an algebraic representation is a monoid homomorphism G → End_k(V). This is only the underlying algebraic carrier of the paper’s continuous or smooth representations; it supplies neither topology nor admissibility.

items.name: Continuous representations and residual semisimplification
items.statement: For a continuous finite-dimensional p-adic representation of a number-field absolute Galois group with a stable lattice over a finite coefficient extension, form the semisimplification of its reduction. Its isomorphism class is independent of the lattice. Keep the finite coefficient field and continuous action visible; this is not a trace-only criterion in characteristic p.

items.name: Non-CM automorphic representation
items.statement: For a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(A_F), non-CM means π is not isomorphic to π⊗(χ∘det) for any nontrivial character χ of F×\A_F×. This is the self-twist condition used in Lemma 2.1, not a condition defined by the desired symmetric-power conclusion.

items.name: Automorphic Galois representation in the paper’s sense
items.statement: For F totally real or CM and ρ:G_F→GL_n(Qpbar) continuous, call ρ automorphic when ρ≅r_{Π,ι} for some RAESDC representation Π over a totally real F, respectively RAECSDC Π over a CM F, and some field isomorphism ι:Qpbar→C. The predicate deliberately includes the essential self-duality or conjugate-self-duality restriction.

items.name: The statement SP_n
items.statement: For positive integer n, SP_n asserts that every non-CM RAESDC representation π of GL₂(A_F), for every totally real number field F, has its (n−1)st symmetric-power transfer, equivalently in the senses of Lemma 2.1. Smaller trivial ranks appearing in the induction must be handled as base conventions, not by constructing GL₀ automorphic representations.

items.name: Geometric reciprocity and Hodge–Tate convention bridge
items.statement: Translate the paper’s Artin reciprocity sending a uniformiser to geometric Frobenius, rec^T(π)=rec(π⊗|det|^((1−n)/2)), and HT(ε_p)=−1 to the atlas’s arithmetic-Frobenius and HT(χ_p)=+1 conventions. Record the inversion/sign conversion for Frobenius and Hodge–Tate labels explicitly. Do not invert an actual determinant character merely because the Hodge–Tate sign convention changes; the multiplier and Tate-twist equations must commute with the chosen representation comparison.

items.name: Residual symmetric power with two constituents
items.statement: For p prime, 0
items.locator: Equation (1.1), repeated at the beginning of §6

items.name: Small-weight Clebsch–Gordan decomposition
items.statement: For a two-dimensional representation V over Fpbar and 1<r<p, V⊗Sym^(r−1)V is isomorphic to Sym^r V ⊕ det(V)⊗Sym^(r−2)V. The r=1 case is V⊗Sym⁰V≅V and has no negative symmetric power.

items.name: One-prime criterion for symmetric-power functoriality
items.statement: For F totally real, π a non-CM RAESDC representation of GL₂(A_F), and n≥1, the following are equivalent: a cuspidal GL_n transfer having parameter Sym^(n−1)rec(π_v) at every place; automorphy of Sym^(n−1)r_{π,ι} for every prime p and every ι; automorphy for some p and some ι. The last implication uses coefficient conjugation, finite-place local–global compatibility and the archimedean Hodge–Tate dictionary, not just equality at unramified places.

items.name: Strong irreducibility
items.statement: A representation ρ of G_F is strongly irreducible when ρ restricted to G_L is irreducible for every finite extension L/F. For a representation of G_{F(ζ_{p∞})}, the same condition quantifies over finite extensions of that field. Do not replace this condition by irreducibility over F alone.

items.name: Strong irreducibility for non-CM Hilbert representations
items.statement: For F totally real and π a non-CM RAESDC representation of GL₂(A_F), each associated r_{π,ι} is strongly irreducible. This is imported in the paper from Newton–Thorne 2023, Example 2.29; its proof is a prior-paper obligation, not supplied here by the definition.

items.name: Unequal-weight tensor irreducibility after cyclotomic restriction
items.statement: Let ρ,ρ′:G_F→GL₂(Qpbar) be continuous and strongly irreducible. Suppose at an embedding τ inducing v|p both restrictions are Hodge–Tate, with weights {a,b} and {a′,b′}, and a−b≠±(a′−b′). For all m,m′≥1, (Sym^mρ⊗Sym^m′ρ′)|G_{F(ζ_{p∞})} is strongly irreducible. The two positive exponents and the unequal weight-difference hypothesis are retained.

items.name: Projective product monodromy from unequal weights
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 2.2, the Zariski closure of (Projρ,Projρ′) is PGL₂×PGL₂. The graph alternative in Goursat’s lemma would identify the two adjoint representations and their labelled Hodge–Tate weights, contradicting the unequal differences. This is a consequence of these rank-two hypotheses, not a general independence theorem for compatible systems.

items.name: Adequacy of small symmetric powers
items.statement: For p≥5 there is a common integer a₀(p)≥3 such that, whenever a≥a₀(p) and a finite subgroup G of GL₂(Fpbar) contains a conjugate of SL₂(F_{p^a}), the image of Sym^(r−1) on G is adequate for every 0<r<p. Adequate means the precise Thorne 2012 Definition 2.3 condition, not merely irreducible or enormous.

items.name: Adequacy of Frobenius-twisted tensors
items.statement: For the same p,a₀(p),a,G as in Lemma 2.3, and every 0<r<p, the image of Frob_p(Std)⊗Sym^(r−1)(Std) on G is adequate. Coefficient Frobenius acts on the first standard factor only.

items.name: Large image after small-index restriction
items.statement: For p≥5, a≥a₀(p) and finite G≤GL₂(Fpbar) containing a conjugate of SL₂(F_{p^a}), every subgroup H≤G of index strictly less than 2p still contains such a conjugate. Consequently the adequacy assertions of Lemma 2.3 apply to H as well.

items.name: Tamely dihedral local representation of prime order
items.statement: Let v be a finite place of a number field, and p an odd prime with q_v≡−1 mod p. An irreducible admissible complex representation π_v of GL₂(F_v) is tamely dihedral of order p if rec(π_v) is induced from a character χ of the Weil group of the unramified quadratic extension F′_v/F_v whose restriction to inertia has order p. Induction is from W_{F′_v} to W_{F_v}; this type-correct direction is made explicit rather than copied from the reversed-looking HTML indices.

items.name: Tamely dihedral representations are supercuspidal
items.statement: Under Definition 2.4, q_v≡−1 mod p and p odd imply the inducing inertia character differs from its unramified quadratic conjugate. Thus the induced two-dimensional Weil representation is irreducible and π_v is supercuspidal. A reducible principal series is not included in this definition.

items.name: Ordinary Galois filtration in cohomological normalisation
items.statement: For ρ:G_F→GL_n(Qpbar) and dominant integral λ=(λ_τ), ordinarity of weight λ means an upper-triangular flag at each v|p with characters ψ_{v,i}, such that x↦ψ_{v,i}(Art_{F_v}(x))·∏_ττ(x)^(λ_{τ,n−i+1}+i−1) has finite order on O_{F_v}× for every i. Art is geometric reciprocity. The finite-order unit factor is part of the condition; the flag is not replaced by a characteristic-polynomial condition.

items.name: Weight-zero Steinberg implies ordinarity
items.statement: Let F be totally real or CM and π RAESDC or RAECSDC of weight zero on GL_n(A_F). If every π_v for v|p is a character twist of Steinberg, then π is ι-ordinary for every ι:Qpbar→C. Weight zero and the condition at every p-adic place are required.

items.name: Coefficient field of a regular algebraic representation
items.statement: For regular algebraic cuspidal π on GL_n(A_F), K_π is the fixed subfield of C of the stabiliser of the isomorphism class of π^∞ under Aut(C). Its normal closure K̃_π has Galois group Γ_π over Q. This construction depends on the finite-part isomorphism class, not a chosen embedding of a single p-adic coefficient field.

items.name: Semilinear coefficient conjugation
items.statement: For γ∈Aut(C), set γπ^∞=C⊗_{C,γ}π^∞, with λ⊗v=1⊗γ⁻¹(λ)v. The group action is inherited from the second factor. Composition satisfies (γδ)π^∞≅γ(δπ^∞); keep the inverse in the tensor relation.

items.name: Rationality over the coefficient field
items.statement: For regular algebraic cuspidal π on GL_n(A_F), its coefficient field K_π is a number field and π^∞ has a model over K_π. This is the specific Clozel Théorème 3.13 input, not the false assertion that every trace-defined representation descends without obstruction.

items.name: Conjugation of regular algebraic cuspidal representations
items.statement: For F a number field, regular algebraic cuspidal π on GL_n(A_F), and γ∈Aut(C), there is a regular algebraic cuspidal representation γπ with finite part γπ^∞. In the RAESDC/RAECSDC applications its associated Galois representations use the transformed embeddings and normalisations of Lemma 5.2.

items.name: Symmetric powers for regular Hilbert modular forms
items.statement: For a totally real field F and non-CM cuspidal π on GL₂(A_F) with every archimedean component essentially square-integrable, and every n≥2, there exists cuspidal Π_n on GL_n(A_F) with rec_{F_v}(Π_{n,v})≅Sym^(n−1)rec_{F_v}(π_v) for every place v, including ramified and infinite places. Regular but non-paritious weights are included via a separate final reduction; a Galois representation is not assumed for those forms.

items.name: Symmetric powers in the conjugate-self-dual CM-field case
items.statement: Let E be a CM field and π a RAECSDC representation of GL₂(A_E) which is not automorphically induced from a quadratic extension. For every n≥2 there is cuspidal Π_n on GL_n(A_E) with rec_{E_w}(Π_{n,w})≅Sym^(n−1)rec_{E_w}(π_w) at every place w. The RAECSDC and non-induced hypotheses are essential; this is not general GL₂ functoriality over arbitrary CM fields.

items.name: All regular-algebraic symmetric powers
items.statement: SP_n holds for all n≥2. For n≥6 choose a prime p≥5 with p<n<2p and r=n−p; the required smaller ranks r−1,r,r+1,p−r are below n, with trivial small-rank conventions. Use the known ranks through five, the local replacement of Corollary 6.2, and Proposition 6.3. This induction does not assume the general tensor-product functoriality conjecture.

items.name: A congruent ordinary companion of weights zero and two
items.statement: Under context S3, construct a single RAESDC σ on GL₂(A_F) which is ι-ordinary, has HT_τ(r_{σ,ι})={0,2} for every τ, determinant ε_p^(−2)ω_p (ω_p the Teichmüller lift of ε_p mod p), residual semisimplification isomorphic to that of π, an unramified Steinberg twist at v₀, and r_{σ,ι}|G_{F_v}~r_{π,ι}|G_{F_v} at every finite v∤p, v≠v₀. All properties concern the same σ; separate existence statements would not suffice.

items.name: Automorphy of the untwisted tensor
items.statement: Under context S3, assume SP_{r−1} and SP_{r+1}, with the r=1 base case treated separately. For any companion σ satisfying all the conditions of weight-three-companion, r_{π,ι}⊗Sym^(r−1)r_{σ,ι} is isomorphic to r_{Π,ι} for an ι-ordinary RAESDC Π on GL_{2r}(A_F). This is a restricted tensor theorem for the prescribed π and σ, not general GL₂×GL_r functoriality.

items.name: Functoriality lifting for a tensor with one factor fixed
items.statement: Let F be totally real, r≥1, p any prime, ι:Qpbar≅C. Let π,π′ be RAESDC on GL₂(A_F) and σ RAESDC on GL_r(A_F). Assume: π and π′ are weight zero and non-CM; their residual representations are isomorphic; the common residual image contains SL₂(F_{p^a}) up to conjugacy for some p^a>5; at each v|p the two rank-two representations are ordinary simultaneously and potentially crystalline simultaneously, and if p=2 both are potentially crystalline; at each finite v∤p, π_v is a Steinberg character twist iff π′_v is; the semisimplified residual tensor image contains a perfect subgroup having an element with 2r distinct eigenvalues; HT_τ(r_{σ,ι})={0,2,…,2r−2} for every τ; r_{π,ι}⊗r_{σ,ι} is automorphic and strongly irreducible; and r_{π′,ι}⊗r_{σ,ι} is irreducible. Then the latter tensor is automorphic. Do not strengthen the text’s remarks about possible weaker hypotheses into a proved theorem.

items.name: Perfect residual subgroup survives soluble base change
items.statement: If a finite residual image contains a perfect subgroup H, then restriction of the Galois representation to a finite soluble extension preserves H in its image. Thus an element of H with 2r distinct eigenvalues remains available for Theorem 4.1. For a soluble tower this follows stage by stage from the trivial image of a perfect group in a soluble quotient; it is not asserted for arbitrary nonsoluble base change.

items.name: Galois representations under complex coefficient conjugation
items.statement: For F totally real or CM, π RAESDC or RAECSDC on GL_n(A_F), γ∈Aut(C), and ι:Qpbar≅C, there is an isomorphism r_{γπ,ι}≅r_{π,γ⁻¹ι}. This acts on the coefficients and embeddings, not on the base-field absolute Galois group.

items.name: Local coefficient conjugation and transformed embeddings
items.statement: With the preceding π and ι, let γ_p∈G_Qp and γ=ιγ_pι⁻¹. Then γ_p(r_{π,ι})≅r_{π,ιγ_p⁻¹}≅r_{π,γ⁻¹ι}≅r_{γπ,ι}, where γ_p acts entrywise on the representation’s coefficients. The inverse in the embedding is retained.

items.name: Coefficient inertia preserves residual semisimplification
items.statement: If γ_ℓ belongs to inertia I_Qℓ, then coefficient conjugation by γ_ℓ does not change the residual semisimplification of a continuous representation with an invariant integral lattice. In Lemma 5.8 this gives bar r_{δγπ,ι_ℓ}≅bar r_{γπ,ι_ℓ} for a lift of δ in coefficient inertia. An arbitrary arithmetic Frobenius lift is not substituted for inertia in this assertion.

items.name: The exponent-two extension F(S)
items.statement: For a totally real number field F and a finite set S of finite places, F(S) is the maximal abelian extension of exponent two unramified at all finite places outside S. No unramified-at-infinity condition is imposed. The paper uses its splitting fields together with, not in place of, the ray class field of modulus (8) times all real places.

items.name: A positive dyadically square generator from ray splitting
items.statement: Let H/F be the ray class field of modulus (8) times all infinite places, with F totally real. If a finite place w of odd residue characteristic splits in H, then its prime ideal is generated by some totally positive λ_w∈O_F which is a square in F_v× at every v|2. Both positivity and the dyadic square condition are used in the reciprocity argument.

items.name: Reciprocity for the two auxiliary splitting conditions
items.statement: Let F be totally real, H the ray class field of modulus (8) times all infinite places, and S a finite set of finite places. Let v,w∤2 be finite places outside S splitting in F(S)H. Then v splits in F(S∪{w}) iff w splits in F(S∪{v}). The proof uses positive dyadic-square generators, the Kummer description after adjoining one ramified place and the product formula for quadratic Hilbert symbols.

items.name: Two dihedral places give large image at every coefficient prime
items.statement: Let F be totally real, M>5 and π RAESDC of weight zero on GL₂(A_F). Suppose primes t₁,t₂>M and finite v₁,v₂ have residue characteristics p₁,p₂>3 unramified in F, the four rational primes p₁,p₂,t₁,t₂ are distinct, and π_{v_i} is tamely dihedral of order t_i. Let S consist of finite v≠v₁,v₂ where π_v ramifies or v ramifies over Q, together with all places above 2 or 3. Assume v₁ splits in F(S∪{v₂}) and v₂ splits in F(S∪{v₁}). Then for every coefficient prime ℓ and every ι_ℓ, bar r_{π,ι_ℓ}(G_F) contains a conjugate of SL₂(F_{ℓ^a}) for some ℓ^a>M. A single dihedral place does not cover its own two exceptional rational primes.

items.name: A regular semisimple element in the perfect tensor image
items.statement: Let ℓ be prime, r≥1 and q₁,q₂ powers of ℓ exceeding max(4r,5). Suppose the combined projective image of two rank-two residual representations contains PSL₂(F_{q₁})×PSL₂(F_{q₂}), as in Lemma 5.8 where their projective fixed fields intersect in degree at most two over F. The combined linear image contains the corresponding SL₂ product; its image in the semisimplified Std⊗Sym^(r−1) representation is perfect and contains an element with 2r distinct eigenvalues. Choose x∈F_{q₂}× of order >2(r−1) and y∈F_{q₁}× avoiding ±x^i for 1−r≤i≤r−1. The size bounds make this avoidance possible.

items.name: Residual twisted tensor witness under global image hypotheses
items.statement: Under context S5-global and SP_{r−1}, SP_r and SP_{r+1}, construct an ι-ordinary RAESDC Π on GL_{2r}(A_F) whose residual representation is Frob_p(bar r_{π,ι})⊗Sym^(r−1)bar r_{π,ι}. The published statement is residual: it does not identify r_{Π,ι} with a coefficient-Frobenius twist of the characteristic-zero tensor. The proof first uses a companion with different Hodge–Tate weights.

items.name: Large residual image from the final local conditions
items.statement: Under context S5-local, bar r_{π,ι}(G_F) contains SL₂(F_{p^a}) up to conjugacy for some p^a>M. This conclusion does not assume any SP_k statement: Lemma 5.3 converts the ordered splitting conditions into those of Proposition 5.4.

items.name: Residual twisted tensor witness retaining a Steinberg place
items.statement: Under context S5-local, assume SP_{r−1}, SP_r and SP_{r+1}. Construct an ι-ordinary RAESDC Π on GL_{2r}(A_F) with bar r_{Π,ι}≅Frob_p(bar r_{π,ι})⊗Sym^(r−1)bar r_{π,ι}. The allowed extra Steinberg place v₁ is retained for the later level-raising theorem. The conclusion is only a residual witness, not full tensor-product functoriality.

items.name: A congruent potentially unramified replacement at the extra place
items.statement: Under context S5-local, construct a congruent ι-ordinary RAESDC π′ with weight zero, determinant ε_p^(−1), unramified Steinberg twists at all p-adic places, and the same local-component data as π at non-p places other than v₁. At v₁ choose a principal series whose character ratio has order p; its residual inertial semisimplification agrees with the original Steinberg representation because q_{v₁}≡1 mod p. Preserve the ramification set and both auxiliary dihedral types so that π′ satisfies the global image hypotheses needed in Theorem 5.5. This replacement is used only to produce the residual witness for π.

items.name: Soluble replacement with all final local conditions
items.statement: Given a totally real F, a non-CM RAESDC π on GL₂(A_F), p≥5 and 0<r<p, construct a soluble totally real extension E/F, ι:Qpbar≅C and a RAESDC π′ over E such that Sym^(p+r−1)r_{π,ι} is automorphic iff Sym^(p+r−1)r_{π′,ι} is. Require π′ weight zero, determinant ε_p^(−1), unramified Steinberg twists at all v|p of E, a tamely dihedral order-p place v₀ with q≡−1 mod p, an unramified Steinberg place v₁ with q≡1 mod p, and potentially unramified local factors at every finite v∤p other than v₁. Also require primes t₁,t₂>p^(a₀(p)) and places w_i of residue characteristics p_i>3 unramified in E, all p₁,p₂,t₁,t₂ distinct, with order-t_i dihedral type at w_i. For H/E of modulus (8) times all infinite places and S the finite ramification/absolute-ramification/2,3 set away from w_i, require w₁ split in HE(S) and w₂ split in HE(S∪{w₁}). These are the joint eight conditions of Proposition 6.1; their proof uses successive congruence primes, not just field restriction.

items.name: Ordinary replacement with a Frobenius-tensor residual witness
items.statement: For totally real F, non-CM RAESDC π, p≥5, 0a₀(p), an unramified Steinberg twist at some v₁∤p, and an ι-ordinary RAESDC GL_{2r} representation whose residual representation is Frob_p(bar r_{π′,ι})⊗Sym^(r−1)bar r_{π′,ι}. The p-adic places here are of E, resolving the mismatched field label in the displayed source statement.

items.name: Symmetric-power lifting from two ordinary residual blocks
items.statement: Let F be totally real, p≥5, 0a₀(p), has weight zero, and has an unramified Steinberg twist at a place v₁∤p. Suppose ι-ordinary RAESDC representations π₁ on GL_{p−r}(A_F) and π₂ on GL_{2r}(A_F) have residual representations Sym^(p−r−1)bar r_{π,ι} and Frob_p(bar r_{π,ι})⊗Sym^(r−1)bar r_{π,ι}, respectively. Then there is ι-ordinary RAESDC Π on GL_{p+r}(A_F) with r_{Π,ι}≅Sym^(p+r−1)r_{π,ι}. The source’s use of Tho24 Proposition 7.4 replaces its TP_r hypothesis by these two explicit residual witnesses; general TP_r is not an input.

items.name: A companion separated from every conjugate coefficient system
items.statement: Under S5-global and SP_{r−1}, SP_r, SP_{r+1}, choose σ as in Lemma 5.6 (the weight-three companion with its untwisted tensor automorphic). Let K_π be the coefficient field of π, K̃_π its Galois closure, Γ_π=Gal(K̃_π/Q), B≥1 such that K_π is ramified only at primes ℓ<B, and φ=ιφ_pι⁻¹. Construct t,ι_t and RAESDC σ′ jointly with: t>max(5,4r+2,B), t unramified in F and all three forms unramified above t; the residual tensors of π and φπ with Sym^(r−1)σ at t are absolutely irreducible; bar r_{σ,ι_t}≅bar r_{σ′,ι_t} and σ′_{v₀} is an unramified Steinberg twist; the tensor of π with Sym^(r−1)σ′ is automorphic and the tensor for φπ with σ is automorphic iff that for φπ with σ′ is; for every ℓ<B and every ι_ℓ, bar r_{σ′,ι_ℓ} has SL₂(F_{ℓ^a}) image with ℓ^a>max(4r,5), and its projective fixed field intersects the one for γπ in degree at most two over F for every γ∈Γ_π. The construction in the proof keeps the companion’s labelled weights {0,2} and appropriate local-component conditions. The congruence σ≡σ′ is at t; a congruence at the original p is not asserted.
items.locator: Lemma 5.7, all five conclusions and construction in its proof

items.name: One inertia step changes only the first tensor factor
items.statement: Under S5-global and the common σ,σ′,B,K̃_π,Γ_π constructed in auxiliary-coefficient-prime-companion, let γ∈Γ_π, let w|ℓ be a finite place of K̃_π and δ∈I_{w/ℓ}. If r_{γπ,ι}⊗Sym^(r−1)r_{σ′,ι} is automorphic, then r_{δγπ,ι}⊗Sym^(r−1)r_{σ′,ι} is automorphic. For δ≠1 only ℓ<B occurs; the proof changes the comparison embedding to one inducing w, applies Theorem 4.1, and returns to ι. The second tensor factor is fixed, not conjugated together with the first.

items.name: Propagation to every conjugate of the first tensor factor
items.statement: Under S5-global and auxiliary-coefficient-prime-companion, r_{γπ,ι}⊗Sym^(r−1)r_{σ′,ι} is automorphic for every γ∈Γ_π. Start from γ=1 and write γ as a product of elements of finite-prime inertia subgroups of Γ_π, using that Q has no nontrivial everywhere-unramified extension. Repeated application of inertia-step-functoriality changes only the first factor. The general inertia-generation/number-field theorem is an imported input, not proved merely by this propagation lemma.
items.locator: §5.2, completion of Theorem 5.5 between Lemma 5.8 and its proof

items.name: Automorphy of the Frobenius-twisted companion tensor
items.statement: Under S5-global and SP_{r−1}, SP_r, SP_{r+1}, for σ supplied by Lemma 5.6 there is an ι-ordinary RAESDC Π on GL_{2r}(A_F) with r_{Π,ι}≅φ_p(r_{π,ι})⊗Sym^(r−1)r_{σ,ι}. Obtain it by taking the coefficient action of φ_p in all-coefficient-conjugates-tensor and applying the σ′-to-σ equivalence of Lemma 5.7, together with Lemma 5.2. Unlike Theorem 5.5’s final residual output, this characteristic-zero statement uses the different-weight companion σ, not π in both factors; its regularity is essential.

items.name: Frobenius on the coefficient field of a residual representation
items.statement: For a rank-two representation over Fpbar, form the representation obtained by applying x↦x^p to matrix coefficients, using the existing Frobenius field automorphism. For an arithmetic Frobenius lift φ_p∈G_Qp its action on the residual coefficients is this construction and is independent of the chosen lift. It is not restriction of the base-field Galois representation or Frobenius at a place of F.
items.locator: Introduction, equation (1.1) and its following parenthesis; Lemma 2.3

items.name: Congruence via residual semisimplification
items.statement: Two continuous semisimple ℓ-adic Galois representations are congruent exactly when the semisimplifications of their reductions are isomorphic. This uses invariant integral lattices and the lattice-independence theorem; it does not require their integral lattices, nonsplit residual extensions or characteristic-zero representations to be isomorphic.

items.name: One threshold for the symmetric-power image conditions
items.statement: For each prime p≥5 choose an integer a₀(p)≥3 for which all three conclusions of Lemma 2.3 hold simultaneously: every finite G⊂GL₂(Fpbar) containing a conjugate of SL₂(F_{p^a}), a≥a₀(p), has adequate Sym^(r−1) image and adequate Frob(Std)⊗Sym^(r−1) image for every 0<r<p, and every subgroup of G of index <2p contains such an SL₂ subgroup. The later strict hypothesis a>a₀(p) is kept where the paper requires it.

items.name: The ray class field with modulus eight and all real places
items.statement: For totally real F, use its ray class field H for the modulus (8) together with every infinite place. Its splitting criterion identifies a split prime with the ray-principal condition, including total positivity and the congruence modulo 8. It is an instance of the existing ray-class-field construction, not a new class field correspondence.

items.name: Quadratic Hilbert reciprocity
items.statement: For a number field F and a,b∈F×, the product of their quadratic Hilbert symbols over all places is 1. Include the real and dyadic factors and finite support. This is the cohomologically normalised ClassFieldTheory formula; Lemma 5.3 applies it to positive dyadic-square prime generators.

items.name: Splitting in a compositum of abelian class fields
items.statement: For finite abelian extensions L₁/F,L₂/F, a finite place unramified in both splits in L₁L₂ iff it splits in each factor. Use the existing Galois/lattice and Artin-splitting maps. The paper uses this for F(S)H and for the further quadratic extension of F(S).
items.locator: Lemma 5.3 hypotheses and proof; Theorem 5.9 proof

items.name: Adjoining the square root of the new prime generator
items.statement: Let F be totally real, S a finite set of finite places, and v∤2 a finite place outside S. Suppose the prime ideal at v is generated by a totally positive λ_v which is a square in every F_u for u|2, as provided by splitting in the modulus-eight-and-infinity ray class field. Then F(S∪{v})=F(S)(√λ_v). The Kummer argument controls ramification at v, at other odd places and at the dyadic places separately; no assumption that F(S) is totally real is added.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.3, description of F(S∪{v})

routes.reason: R16.3 already owns explicit rank-two local Langlands formulas and supercuspidal examples, and R16.4 owns the global GL2 representation comparisons. Add Definition 2.4 and its supercuspidality consequence, and the self-twist formulation of non-CM, as source-specific declarations there. Import the generic local correspondence and finite-group/Weil carriers; do not introduce a second automorphic representation definition.

ML.3 explicitly plans Newton–Thorne symmetric-power automorphy. The companion, two residual-witness constructions, ordered auxiliary-place replacements and final induction are source-specific proof obligations of that existing endpoint, not a second roadmap. ML.5 owns selected tensor-product functoriality and receives the exact Theorem 4.1; ML.0 owns its normalization dictionary. The generic local/global deformation rings, patching modules, higher-rank ordinary theory and compatible systems remain imports. Sections 3 and 4 still require declaration-level internal decompositions listed in remaining.

R01.1, R01.4 and G7 own continuous coefficient operations, rank-two residual image applications and dimension-general symmetric/tensor image criteria. The paper adds the specific semisimplified decomposition, Frobenius-tensor adequacy, unequal-Hodge-difference irreducibility, perfect-subgroup argument and all-primes residual-image criterion. Reuse algebraic representation, field Frobenius and group-theoretic suppliers; do not identify adequate with enormous or claim a new generic representation carrier.

The arbitrary-rank full-flag ordinary functor is already within L7. Definition 2.5(2) is an exact source for its character and labelled-weight convention. Compare with the determinant-ordinary condition from L8 rather than replacing flags by characteristic polynomials; the automorphic ordinary predicate and its theorem are separate consumers.

PA.2 owns general-rank CM/unitary ordinary constructions and their arithmetic comparison, unlike the rank-two ordinary modular/Hilbert roadmap. Use Lemma 2.6 as a source-qualified weight-zero Steinberg-to-ordinary application with its coefficient-prime local–global comparison input. This route does not assert that PA.2 already proves the new tensor functoriality theorem or that a unit Hecke eigenvalue alone gives an ordinary Galois flag.

AG2.0 explicitly owns fields of rationality versus realization and normalization, and AG2.6 owns compatible systems and coefficient embeddings. Add the exact Clozel field-of-definition result recalled as Theorem 5.1 and the two coefficient-conjugation formulas of Lemma 5.2 as sources for those existing stages. These are not a general assertion that every trace-defined representation descends.

R02.3 owns restricted-ramification Galois groups and finite-coefficient arithmetic finiteness. Add the exponent-two field F(S) and the one-new-ramified-place Kummer calculation used in Lemma 5.3 as precise applications, importing class fields and quadratic Hilbert reciprocity from their existing upstream owner. F(S) may ramify at infinity and the set S is as in the paper; do not silently impose a different unramified-at-infinity condition. No new class field correspondence or generic duality carrier is planned.
